name: Avoiding methane emissions through composting at DN Agrar, Romania
description:
The “Avoiding Methane Emissions through Composting at DN Agrar, Romania” project aims to significantly reduce greenhouse gas emissions by implementing controlled aerobic composting of raw dairy manure at two farms located in Alba and Hunedoara counties. Traditionally, manure is managed through open stockpiling or storage in lagoons, practices that lead to uncontrolled anaerobic decomposition and the release of methane (CH₄), a greenhouse gas with a global warming potential significantly higher than CO₂.

By diverting manure from these conventional methods and instead processing it through a structured composting system, the project prevents methane emissions at source. The composting process stabilizes the organic material, producing high-quality compost that can be applied to agricultural land. This not only improves soil health and fertility but also enhances the soil’s carbon sequestration capacity, supporting long-term climate resilience in Romanian agriculture.

In summary, the project delivers both immediate climate benefits through methane avoidance and broader environmental co-benefits by promoting sustainable manure management and improving local soil systems.
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals

name: JACA MBE ARR Congo
description:
The project aims to plant approximately 40,000 hectares of Acacia mangium in degraded grasslands within a two-area concession in the Pool district, Republic of Congo (Brazzaville). Additionally, it seeks to reforest 4,000 hectares of native forest, contributing to the restoration of the original forest cover remnants in the area. 
Furthermore, the project includes the integration of Agroforestry systems (AFS), which have the potential to incorporate various elements, including fruit trees, transforming these areas into versatile orchards. 
Moreover, the initiative plans to implement agriculture intensification programs, such as high-yield Cassava, to enhance food security access and alleviate the pressure of shifting agriculture on the landscape. 
To address energy needs, the project will introduce energy plantations and provide technical and material support for establishing plantations of rapidly growing species like Eucalyptus or Acacia sp. This approach aims to improve access to fuelwood and reduce pressure on this resource across the landscape. 
Simultaneously, the project strives to enhance the livelihoods of local communities by creating job opportunities and offering technical and material support for small-scale business activities, such as apiculture and mushroom cultivation, in collaboration with stakeholders.

name: METHANE EMISSION REDUCTION BY AWD IN RICE FARMING IN CAMBODIA-VPA02
description: This VPA aims to save water and reduce methane emissions during rice farming by introducing water management technology to rice farming, which is one of the main greenhouse gas emission sources in Takeo of Cambodia. By participating in this project, farmers can produce low-carbon rice without reducing rice productivity and participate in mitigating climate change. ThanksCarbon, a business developer, has introduced an AI-based satellite technology into this project to reduce the burden on individual farmers for data collection and improve the convenience of monitoring data collection and MRV transparency. Farmers will be motivated and trained to refrain from continuously flooding their fields by putting the suggested AWD technology into effect, which would cut down on the quantity of CH4 emissions that would have been produced in the baseline situation. The sole change made to the project scenario is the adoption of alternating wetting and drying conditions rather than the submerged condition. Other than that, the project keeps the current agricultural techniques in place and does not introduce any new activities that might increase greenhouse gas emissions.
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals

name: GS12602 GS12677 RVPA-1 Powerstove Multiple Fuel Project
description:
The main purpose of the project activity is the distribution of fuel-efficient improved
cook stoves (ICS) specifically in the states of Nigeria. The Improved cook-stoves distributed through this project has replaced the low-efficient traditional cook-stoves. Through this project, the distribution and installation of high thermal efficient improved cook stoves (ICS) has been undertaken for households. The ICS burns non-renewable woody biomass and/or charcoal more efficiently thereby improving thermal energy transfer to pots, hence saving fuel wood and greenhouse gases. Not only will this halt the rapidly progressing deforestation but will also reduce health hazards from indoor air (smoke) pollution and women and children will have to spend less time collecting firewood.

name: University of Guam Sustainable Reforestation and Carbon Offset Initiative
description:
The Ugum Watershed Reforestation and Carbon Offset Initiative targets 100 acres (~40.5 hectares) of degraded, non-forested savanna land in Southern Guam, within the villages of Inalåhan and Talo’fo’fo’. While the site has been undergoing restoration since 2019 under the Guam Restoration of Watersheds (GROW) initiative, only plantings occurring after April 7, 2023 are eligible for carbon crediting under this project. 
The site plays a critical ecological role: it feeds into the Ugum River, which is essential for the southern municipal water supply. Restoration activities reduce erosion, improve water quality, and enhance forest cover to buffer against the region’s susceptibility to fire, storm events, and flash flooding.
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals
project_developer: University of Guam Center for Island Sustainability & Sea Grant (UOG CIS & SG)

name: Producción sostenible de biofertilizantes y biogás a partir de desechos de materia orgánica. Gran Canaria
description:
The plant, located in the municipality of Agüimes, in Gran Canaria, is expected to come into operation in October 2025, at which time a three-month operational test phase will be carried out to guarantee the efficiency and safety of the process. The implementation to obtain emission reductions is estimated in the first quarter of 2026.
This first plant will be located next to the Southeast treatment plant, in the port free zone of Gran Canaria, which will facilitate its logistical integration and connectivity with distribution channels. It will be designed to manage up to 31,000 tonnes of organic waste per year, from which approximately 2,242 tonnes of biomethane per year will be produced, equivalent to 31,141 MWh of energy. This production of this energy vector represents a sustainable alternative to about 2,832 tons of propane gas, which will allow a significant reduction in the use of fossil fuels and polluting gas emissions and contribute to local climate and energy governance. 
As for the size and scope of the activity of the facility, it is estimated that it can serve some 45-65 hotels since the capacity of the digester, is 31,000 t/y of organic waste.
Among the key components of the project, the production of biomethane as a renewable substitute for propane gas and diesel stands out.
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals

name: Agroforestry for Livelihoods and Climate Resilience in Odisha: A Joint Initiative by Infosys and SGI Foundation
description:
The proposed initiative is a Voluntary Project Activity (VPA) focused on agroforestry plantations, to be implemented in Odisha, India. Implemented by the SGI Foundation, the project aims to sequester atmospheric carbon dioxide through large-scale plantation activities, while simultaneously enhancing local biodiversity, improving soil health, and promoting sustainable livelihoods. The project emphasizes the cultivation of native and climate-resilient agroforestry species such as Mango, Teak, Cashew, Jackfruit, Guava, and other regionally suitable trees under the first VPA. Active participation from local farmers is central to the initiative, empowering them to adopt agroforestry practices that improve income security and resilience to climate variability.
Beyond its environmental benefits, the project contributes significantly to socio-economic development by generating temporary employment for community members during the plantation's establishment and maintenance phases. It also strengthens long-term sustainability through capacity-building and inclusive community engagement. The initiative supports multiple SDGs, including Climate Action (SDG 13), Life on Land (SDG 15), and No Poverty (SDG 1), by integrating carbon sequestration with biodiversity conservation and rural development. A core objective of the project is to quantify the carbon sequestration potential of agroforestry plantations in Odisha while uplifting farming communities through sustainable land-use practices.
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals
poa_project_name: Agroforestry for Livelihoods and Climate Resilience in India: A Joint Initiative by Infosys and SGI Foundation

name: Accelerating Access to Clean Cooking in Kenya by Nyalore Impact Limited
description:
The proposed project activity ‘Accelerating Access to Clean Cooking in Kenya Project by Nyalore Impact Limited’ will be implemented by Nyalore Impact Limited’ with the purpose of promoting and distributing clean cooking devices that include Induction Cookers (ICs) and Electric Pressure Cookers (EPCs) to house-holds in Kenya. The project intends to accelerate access to clean cooking by displacing use of inefficient biomass cooking devices and polluting fuels. Use of the project technology will displace GHG emissions from the thermal energy consumption required for cooking by households. This will consequently contribute towards reduced household air pollution and support several sustainable development goals. The project’s primary target is end-users who cook using inefficient biomass cookstoves and polluting fuels such as kerosene both in the urban and rural areas of Kenya.

Goals and Objectives of the Project Activity
According to the 2022 KNBS Demographic and Health Survey (DHS) report, 68.5% of Kenyan population still highly dependent on traditional cooking fuels, with firewood being the predominant cooking fuel. This presents a climate change challenge and has motivated the project developer to develop an innovative project that will accelerate the transition to cleaner cooking solutions to mitigate the negative impacts associated with the use of traditional fuels.
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals

By replacing traditional open-fire cooking methods with improved cookstoves, the project will significantly reduce fuel consumption, thereby decreasing deforestation rates and promoting the sustainable management of natural resources. The project aligns with the Gold Standard's objectives of delivering real, measurable, and long-term emission reductions and promoting sustainable development benefits.
